seoDescription: Interactive map of the best baguettes in Paris with winners, finalists and addresses by year.
aboutIntroLead: Paris has its official best baguette contest, highlighting bakers, addresses, and baking know-how every year.
aboutIntroBody: Each year, the contest pits baguettes from Paris bakers against one another. A top ten ranking is established, and the winner receives a medal, a **4,000 euro prize**, and becomes the **Elysee Palace supplier** for one year.
aboutRouteCta: Find the nearest bakery on foot
aboutRouteMobileCta: Find the best bakery closest to you
aboutIntroDetail: The jury includes professionals, food journalists, and **Paris residents selected by lot**. The baguettes are presented anonymously to limit bias during tasting.
aboutSubjective: This ranking does not necessarily mean it is objectively the single best baguette for everyone. Taste remains partly subjective, and the map can simply be used as a practical tool to try good addresses and compare them for yourself.

aboutCriteria: The selected baguettes must also meet several technical criteria. They are judged on **baking, crumb, taste, smell, and appearance**. The rules have evolved over time: historically, baguettes had to measure between 55 and 65cm and weigh between 250 and 300g; for the recent 2025 and 2026 editions, the City of Paris instead indicates 50 to 55cm and 250 to 270g, with a maximum salt content of 1.4g per 100g of bread, so that the products are compared within a common framework.
aboutFactSinceBody: The full winners list available on a single map.
aboutFactYearBody: Winner, finalists, and addresses accessible in just a few clicks.
aboutFactParisBody: A practical starting point for exploring a neighborhood with a baguette in hand.
aboutWhyBody: The contest is well known, but its archives are scattered. Some years are easy to find, others much less so. This map helps bring some order to it, makes the ranking easier to read, and helps anyone who really wants to see whether a baguette is worth the detour.

walkRouteDistanceInfo: This number corresponds both to the amount of baguettes laid end to end to cover that distance and to a very theoretical estimate of calories burned while walking it.
walkRouteDistanceInfoBaguette: The baguette number is the number of baguettes laid end to end to cover that distance. The calculation uses 1 baguette = 55cm.
walkRouteDistanceInfoCalories: The calorie number is a very theoretical estimate of calories burned while walking this route. It assumes flat walking, a 70kg adult, and the route pace when it is known, otherwise an average walking pace of about 4.8km/h. As a rough reference, one traditional baguette of about 250g is around 700kcal.
walkRouteDurationInfo: This number is a theoretical order of magnitude for how many baguettes could be produced in France during the time it would take you to reach the bakery. The estimate is based on an annual average of more than 6 billion baguettes, or about 11,416 per minute, while real production varies depending on the time of day and bakery schedules.
